title: The stamp takes the room, then the card

members.role: the chart is the world - the page lands on its axes and its lines draw before anything is added to it
the named thing ('Data centers') is added to the world bare - a catalogued cutout, no card chrome
it comes down on its word into the page's biggest free room, off-square, the ring hugging it - fitted FIRST in the row (row_stamp_fits, P69 T5)
the record that proves it (the leases filing) lands in the room left, clear of the mark and of its ring's widest disc - stamp_clash_error refuses any box that touches them

does: A named thing is stamped into the page's biggest free room on its word; later the record that proves it lands in the room left, clear of the mark and its ring - the stamp chooses first and the card goes round it.

use_when.shape: a named thing + the record that proves it, over a held chart
use_when.use: a sentence that names a physical thing ('Data centers') and then points at its source ('right there in the filing'): the prop into the biggest room on the name, the record in the room left on the source word
use_when.dont: a prop inside a card (props are bare), a record the page has no room for (place it by hand clear of the ring, or park the chart), or a light instead of the arrival (E99 s71)

source: P69 T35 (the operator 2026-09-22) over P69 T5's stamp-plus-card row (tests/test_the_stamp_arrival.py); proved as a beat by projects/_proofs/p69-recipes/proof_p69_recipes.py on Steel and Paper H row 16 ('Go into the filings ... right there in the filing', take 303.34 s) on ev-debt-issuance-line-v1 with prop-hyperscale-datacenter-v1 and ev-doc-leases - no approved cut carries it
